title: Gap Appoints New Athleta CEO, Cuts Full-Year Guidance Amid Retail Challenges
body:
Gap Inc. announced a leadership change for its Athleta division on Thursday, naming longtime executive Ashley Kechter as the brand’s next president and chief executive officer, effective Dec. 14. The appointment comes as the retailer disclosed a mixed set of results for its fiscal third quarter, prompting a modest reduction in its full‑year earnings outlook. The move signals Gap’s intent to refocus Athleta’s growth strategy amid a competitive active‑wear market and lingering challenges in its core Gap and Banana Republic lines.  

Kechter, who has spent more than a decade at Gap Inc., most recently served as senior vice president of global product and merchandising for Athleta. In that role, she oversaw the brand’s product development, sourcing, and design teams, helping to expand its size‑inclusive offerings and sustainability initiatives. Her deep familiarity with Athleta’s operational DNA is expected to accelerate the rollout of new product categories and digital enhancements that the company believes are essential to capture a broader, younger consumer base. “Athleta is at a pivotal moment where we can leverage our brand equity in performance‑plus‑fashion and translate that into sustained profitable growth,” Kechner said in an internal memo, adding that her focus will be on “innovation, inclusive sizing, and a seamless omnichannel experience.”  

The leadership shift occurs against a backdrop of uneven financial performance. Gap Inc. reported third‑quarter revenue of $2.2 billion, roughly in line with analysts’ expectations, but earnings per share fell short, driven by weaker sales at its flagship Gap banner and heightened promotional activity. The company trimmed its full‑year adjusted earnings guidance from $2.20–$2.30 per share to $2.10–$2.20, citing “persistent macro‑economic headwinds” and “elevated inventory levels” as primary constraints. While Athleta posted a 10 percent year‑over‑year sales increase, its contribution was insufficient to offset the drag from the other two brands, which together posted a combined 4 percent decline.  

Industry observers note that Athleta’s growth trajectory has outpaced its peers in the active‑wear segment, thanks to its emphasis on athleisure that blends performance fabrics with fashion‑forward designs. However, the market is crowded, with rivals such as Lululemon, Nike, and emerging direct‑to‑consumer labels intensifying price competition and innovation cycles. Kechner’s appointment is therefore seen as a strategic effort to sharpen Athleta’s differentiation, particularly through expanded plus‑size offerings and a stronger sustainability narrative—areas where the brand has already earned consumer goodwill. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate that a successful execution of these initiatives could lift Athleta’s contribution margin by up to 150 basis points over the next 12 months.  

Beyond product strategy, Gap Inc. is also betting on digital transformation to revive its overall performance. The retailer plans to invest an additional $200 million in its e‑commerce platforms, with a focus on AI‑driven personalization and faster fulfillment. Kechner is expected to collaborate closely with the company’s chief digital officer to integrate Athleta’s online experience more tightly with its brick‑and‑mortar footprint, particularly in high‑traffic urban centers such as New York City, where a flagship Athleta store recently opened in Times Square. The synergy between digital and physical channels is viewed as a critical lever to boost same‑store sales and reduce inventory turnover.  

Looking ahead, Gap Inc. will monitor the impact of Kechner’s leadership during the upcoming holiday season, a traditionally strong sales period for active‑wear. The company’s revised outlook suggests a cautious optimism: while overall revenue growth may remain modest, the firm hopes that Athleta’s accelerated momentum will serve as a catalyst for broader turnaround. Investors will be watching closely for signs that the new CEO can translate strategic intent into measurable results, especially as the retailer navigates a challenging retail environment marked by shifting consumer preferences and lingering supply‑chain uncertainties. If Kechner can deliver on her growth agenda, Athleta could emerge as the engine that steadies Gap Inc.’s financial health and positions the conglomerate for a more resilient future.
